thread:
neha: heads-up — saw route oscillation in us-west during the spike this morning. looks correlated with probe sampling hitting ~4% and then the policy engine aggressively reweighing tenants. wondering if our sampling -> immediate weight update is too twitchy.
micah: can you paste the short logs? are you seeing many small successful probes flip a route weight down?
neha: yeah, pattern is: a few slow probe latencies (normal variance), probes mark region as degraded, weight drops 30%, traffic shifts, probes then see lower queue and mark healthy, weight jumps back. repeats. pasted minimal trace: ```
[2026-02-26T09:12:01Z] probe(us-west): p50=35ms p95=220ms
[2026-02-26T09:12:04Z] policy: weight(us-west)=0.7 -> 0.49 (deprioritize)
[2026-02-26T09:12:10Z] probe(us-west): p50=18ms p95=45ms
[2026-02-26T09:12:11Z] policy: weight(us-west)=0.49 -> 0.72 (reward)
```
micah: ugh. that's the classic sampling feedback loop. two quick options: (A) smooth probe metric before feeding to policy, (B) separate sampling rate from weight-change rate (i.e. sample high, apply weight updates slower / with hysteresis).
jorge: we also need to decide who owns smoothing. Currently probes live in runtime sidecars and the policy engine just consumes probe events. If we implement smoothing in runtime sidecars we avoid extra load on policy, but then we duplicate logic across runtimes. If smoothing lives in policy, policy becomes heavyweight and stateful.
sam: one design I want to throw in: move to a "probe-telemetry" stream that publishes raw probes, then a small stateless aggregator service computes short-window EWMA and exposes an API the policy engine queries at decision time. That keeps policy simple and avoids runtime duplication.
micah: EWMA approach looks good; needed params: window (s), alpha, and a separate "dirty" threshold that prevents tiny fluctuations from changing weights. also need a max delta per-update to avoid >30% swings.
neha: agreed on max-delta limit. also recommend tie-breaker: require N consecutive probe-derived signals before flipping a weight if tenant traffic > X rps. for low-traffic tenants, be more permissive.
jorge: edge cases: what about region-level outages where probes stop returning? aggregator must supply explicit 'unknown' and policy should have a fallthrough (fallback pool) rather than oscillate. also need TTL for stale probe data.
sam: sketching a config snippet we could land for a canary: ```yaml
probe_aggregator:
  ewma_alpha: 0.2
  sampling_window_s: 30
  dirty_threshold_ms: 50
  max_weight_delta: 0.25   # relative (0.25 == 25%)
  consecutive_samples_required: 3
  stale_ttl_s: 120
policy_engine:
  apply_mode: "conservative" # immediate | conservative
  conservative_backoff_ms: 200
```
micah: keep in mind we must expose metrics for smoothing decisions (how often we block a change, current EWMA per region) so SRE can debug.
neha: right — also want a short-term sticky window on the runtime side: if a route weight was lowered due to degrade, don't auto-raise above previous baseline for X seconds without manual override. keeps rapid ping-pong down.
jorge: that sticky idea is runtime-friendly and minimal: runtime keeps last_applied_weight with ttl and rejects upward adjustments above last_applied_weight + small epsilon until ttl expires. avoids policy needing to store lots of history.
sam: that splits responsibility: aggregator -> authoritative smoothed signals, policy -> decision rules + max-delta, runtime -> stickiness + enforcement. seems balanced. any objections?
micah: one worry: more moving parts = more deployment complexity. prefer prototype as feature flag gated and only enabled for a small tenant cohort.
neha: agreed. canary plan: 1) deploy aggregator helm chart to staging, 2) enable conservative policy mode behind feature flag for 10% tenants in us-west, 3) runtime sticky window default 30s, 4) gather metrics for 24h.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: probe-aggregator v0.1 -> staging at 2026-02-27T02:00Z. reaction :rocket:
sam: I'll open a short RFC doc with the design split and the proposed config defaults, and include rollback playbook. tagging @micah @neha @jorge for review.
neha: thanks — prioritizing this after the current backfill work. @sam ping me when RFC link lands. :thumbsup:
